title: Evidence Digest static API
description: The complete set of files the pipeline writes under data/api/ and data/feeds/. These are plain files served by GitHub Pages - there is no application server in the read path, which is what makes public browsing free and unlimited. Paths are relative to the deployed site root.

studyCard.$comment: The trimmed study shape used by every list surface (topic files, highlights) and by the email worker. It is `study.schema.json` MINUS `abstract`, `sections`, `mesh`, and `keywords`. Those four fields are omitted because with ~149 topics rebuilt daily, carrying abstracts in every topic file would multiply the served payload roughly tenfold for data only the detail view ever reads - and the detail view gets it from api/days/<date>.json instead. Mirrors `StudyCard` in shared/types.ts.

manifest.$comment: api/manifest.json - fetched first by the web app and by the email worker. Everything else is discovered from here.

dataVersion.description: Bumped when a breaking change lands in the study shape. Clients refuse to render an unknown major version and show a refresh prompt instead.

windowDays.description: How many days of entryDate history the api/ tree covers. Older studies stay in data/studies/ but are not served.

days.description: Every entryDate present in the served window, newest first. Each has a matching api/days/<date>.json.

topicCounts.description: topicSlug -> number of studies in the served window. Drives the counts next to each checkbox in the topic picker.

topicFile.$comment: api/topics/<topicSlug>.json - one file per topic. The web app fetches only the topics a reader selected, so a narrow interest downloads very little.

total.description: Total studies for this topic in the served window, before the per-file cap.

returned.description: How many are actually in this file (capped by scoring.json.limits.perTopicFile).

studies.description: Newest entryDate first; ties broken by score descending, then pmid. Each item is a LEAN CARD, not a full record - see the studyCard definition.

dayFile.$comment: api/days/<date>.json - everything indexed on one day, for the archive view and for email digests that need an exact date range.

highlightsFile.$comment: api/highlights.json - the homepage 'what matters this week' set: top-scoring studies across all specialties over the last 7 days, deduplicated and capped per specialty so one busy field cannot dominate.

studies.description: Lean cards, matching shared/types.ts HighlightsFile.studies: StudyCard[].

searchIndexFile.$comment: api/search-index.json - compact global index over high-signal studies only, so full-text-ish search works without shipping every abstract. Keys are short to keep the file small over the wire.

minScore.description: Only studies scoring at or above this are indexed globally. Searching inside selected topics uses the full topic files instead and is unaffected.

publicTaxonomyFile.$comment: api/taxonomy.json - the reader-facing slice of pipeline/config/taxonomy.json. Match rules are deliberately stripped: they are large, they are an implementation detail, and shipping them would invite gaming.

publicJournalsFile.$comment: api/journals.json - powers the Sources page. Readers can see exactly which journals are watched, which is the whole basis for trusting the digest.

feeds.$comment: feeds/<topicSlug>.xml and feeds/all.xml - Atom 1.0. These exist so the product is fully usable with zero credentials and zero email: point any reader at a topic feed and you have a working alert.
